title: Head 5 · Scene understanding
subtitle: Stages scene and small_objects (Option A): naming what is in each kept frame, where it is and what the wearer is doing, in one record and one caption.
meta: Built and in use on the Pixel 9 Pro XL. Cut-offs are model defaults or card starting values (gap G2).

YOLOX-Tiny, D-FINE S Objects365, MobileCLIP place and action phrases, YOLOE-11L for keys and earbuds and its MobileCLIP gate, the scene record and caption; the VLM and open-vocabulary detectors that were tried.
EYKO-9 (Option A), EYKO-10 (scene record), EYKO-32 (small objects), EYKO-60 (first-person actions), EYKO-63 (YOLOE gate); later: EYKO-25 (Option B), EYKO-26 (Option C).
Head 5 · Scene understanding: describing each kept frame

sections.title: Summary
blocks: Each kept frame is described by four small models instead of one large VLM:

rows: Softmax of 100 × cosine; kept if share ≥ 0.30; actions smoothed over ±6 s
The user's own keys and earbuds
640 px, six words fixed at export, score ≥ 0.25; only on frames MobileCLIP flags

blocks: Their answers are merged into one **scene record** per frame and a short **caption** that always names personal things first. The path to this set was measured step by step: the first detector could not see keys or wallets at all, VLMs were too slow, word-prompted detectors were accurate but slow, and the final mix gives the most finds for the time on the phone.

steps: YOLOX-Tiny lists COCO objects and counts people.
D-FINE S lists Objects365 objects; its "person" is ignored because YOLOX counts people.
The two lists are merged: same name and box overlap > 0.5 means one thing.

MobileCLIP compares the frame's saved 512-d vector with 9 place phrases and 14 action phrases written from the wearer's point of view. The shares of frames within 6 s are averaged before the action is chosen, so one odd frame does not flip the action.
The caption is written: personal things (keys, wallet, glasses, pen, phone…) always first, other things up to 3, then people, place and action. Saved in scene_records.
The gate: if the frame's MobileCLIP cosine to "a photo of keys" or "a photo of earbuds" is at least 0.15, the frame goes to YOLOE; otherwise it is skipped.
YOLOE-11L looks for six words fixed when the model was exported and keeps keys and earbuds (what D-FINE never names).
Finds join the frame's record with source "own" and the caption is written again.

sections.title: Options considered: the path to the current set

blocks.h3: Step 1 · YOLOX-Nano vs YOLOX-Tiny (13 Oct, 44 Pixel frames)

blocks: Nano found 4 of 32 everyday non-person things; Tiny found 18 of 32. People 40 of 40. Phone and laptop agreed (same things on 41 of 44 frames). **Tiny adopted.** Cost with the saved image vector: median 119 ms per frame (Nano path); Tiny about 244 ms.

blocks.h3: Step 2 · The problem: the user's own things

blocks: COCO's 80 classes contain no keys, wallet, glasses or earbuds. Captions said "bench and bird" or "dog". Two ways to look closer were tried on EPIC-KITCHENS take / put events first:

rows: 20 to 33 of 44, but several wrong objects per frame and 18 MobileCLIP runs

blocks.h3: Step 3 · Small VLMs on the laptop (Option C, 44 phone frames)

blocks: Better captions, but too slow to run on every kept frame for now. Kept for later (EYKO-26).

blocks.h3: Step 4 · Detectors asked by word (laptop, own50: 87 labelled own-thing sightings)

blocks: OWLv2 8-bit on the Pixel took 8–13 s a frame, 4.9 GB, with scores up to 0.32 lower than the laptop. OWL-ViT was fast (0.7 s) but found 0 of 22 keys.
D-FINE S found 37 of 87 at 0.37 s on the laptop: wallet 10/16, glasses 9/13, pen 10/12, no false alarms, but never keys or earbuds. On the Pixel 0.96 s per frame with the same scores.

blocks.h3: Step 6 · Combinations on the Pixel (15 Oct, 75 s clip with 13 kept frames)

blocks: YOLOE-11L on the Pixel: 2.34 s per frame, 570 MB native memory, exactly the laptop's scores. **D-FINE + YOLOE adopted, replacing OWLv2** (commit 903b1f9).

bullets: **First-person actions (EYKO-60):** wearer's-view wording, 6 more actions, ±6 s smoothing. MQ F1 10.8 → 32.2 on set A, 15.4 → 16.7 on held-out set B. "Use phone" found 0 → 34.8 %. Kept.
**YOLOE gate (EYKO-63):** YOLOE only where MobileCLIP cosine ≥ 0.15 to keys or earbuds. YOLOE runs on 15–20 % of Ego4D frames; all 18 right finds on our own clips kept. Kept.
